# The challenge: training DRCs {.smaller .center}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
We are seeing a **computational turn in research**, as seen in a

- growing number of research that relies on **data** or **research software** [@crouch2013],

- adoption of **computational methods** by fields that didn't traditionally use them (e.g. computational social sciences, digital humanities...)

- growing importance of **OpenScience** and expectation to manage data and outputs following **FAIR principles**,

- growing number of infrastructure and professionals needed for its delivery,

- the advent of AI (adding a new level of complexity).

This **requires a broad set of skills -[Digital Research Competencies(DRC)]{.highlight-text}-** that need to be [learnt]{.highlight-text} and [taught]{.highlight-text}.
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![[DIRECT Framework](https://directframework.com/) [@nenadic2026]](/media/DIRECT%20Framework_alpha.png)
:::
:::::

::: notes
Research is becoming increasingly computational, as seen in

This requires a broad set skills -Digital Research Competencies- that need to be learnt and taught.

DIRECT framework acknowledges the importance and diversity of training and Digital Research Competencies, but it does not explain some of the questions that we were having...
:::

# So we wondered...

::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
- If training is needed, and RSEs are not doing it, [who are the professionals filling this gap]{.highlight-text}?

- If multiple professionals are doing it: [does the]{.highlight-text} [training differ based on their backgrounds?]{.highlight-text}

- And more broadly: how are DRC being delivered and what are their [key defining]{.highlight-text} [factors]{.highlight-text}?
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![[RSE International Survey](https://rse-survey.soton.ac.uk/superset/dashboard/RSE_survey/) [@HettrickRSESurveylongitudinal2026] (results from 2022 and UK only)](/media/RSE-survey_UK_2022_what-are-you-spending-your-time-on-2026-06-18T11-18-14.266Z.jpg)
:::
:::::

::: notes
For example, after seeing the RSE international Survey, and how training was tangential to RSEs, we wondered...
:::

# Our research {.smaller background-color="#DAD6CA"}

***"Mapping and evaluating dRTP’s contributions to computing skills and pedagogies in Higher Education"*** **is a project funded by the UKRI's [DisCouRSE Network+](https://discourse-network.github.io/) and [aims to map and analyse the provision of digital researchcompetencies (DRC)]{.highlight-text} which are led by or involve dRTP’s across Higher Education institutions in the UK.**

::::: {.columns .smaller}
::: {.column width="70%"}
The research acknowledges and complements existing competency frameworks like DIRECT but [examines the material conditions of training delivery]{.highlight-text} instead of learning needs.

**Research questions include:**

- How are dRTPs engaging in the teaching of Digital Research Competencies?

- What are the methodologies and technologies used to deliver the training? How are decisions on training delivery made?

- How is the training influenced by matters such as type of professional, career stage, background, pedagogical approaches, trends, availability, licences or teachers’ beliefs?

- Are there any approaches that are more frequently used for specific audiences or cases?
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](/media/DisCouRSE-Logo-Light.svg){width="400"} [This work was supported by the [DisCouRSE Network+](https://discourse-network.github.io/), which received funding through the UKRI Digital Research Infrastructure Programme]{.caption}
:::
:::::

::: notes
The research acknowledges and complements existing competency frameworks like DIRECT but examines the material conditions of training delivery instead on learning needs.
:::

# Methodology

## Survey {.smaller}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="70%"}
**People**

- Who are involved? What are their job titles?

- How are they involved in the teaching?

- Do they have any [pedagogical background]{.highlight-text}?

- What are their [beliefs]{.highlight-text} in relation to tech and pedagogy? *(e.g. stance as a teacher, importance of opensource, AI, licences...)*

**Training and pedagogies**

- What is being taught?

- What [formats]{.highlight-text} and [delivery mode]{.highlight-text} are used?

- What are the [key factors]{.highlight-text} influencing how the training is delivered?

- Infrastructure needed

- Challenges
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![Link to the survey: <https://tinyurl.com/DRTP-training-survey>](media/qualtrics-qrcode.png)

EXPLAIN WHERE THE SURVEY WAS DISTRIBUTED TO
:::
:::::

## Systematic analysis + Interviews {.center}

- Computationally map dRTP's across UK HE via web-scraping

- Capture dRTP role descriptions and involvement in training/teaching

- Data to supplement qualitative research;

    - Designed to provide a broad overview of sector wide trends

    - However, not comprehensive! Many dRTP's and their involvement in teach/training not on university webpages/publicly available

## Systematic analysis methods {.centre}

- First attempt; use CommonCrawl as an archive of university webpages

    - Roadblock, CommonCrawl was nowhere near comprehensive enough for this task!

- Currently running;

    - Custom web scraper (*politely*) works through all webpages (branching of homepage) of each UK university

    - Raw HTML is filtered for any potentially relevant content

    - Cleaned HTML passed to LLM and transformed into structured data

## Next steps {.centre}

- Clean and parse systematic analysis results

- Estimate accuracy of results by comparing them against human classified data (University of Warwick)

- Publish aggregate data on github for others to use

- Interviews to follow up on findings from survey and systematic analysis

# Preliminary Results

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(forcats)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(scales)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(treemapify)
library(knitr)


fix_research_typo <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) return(x)
  
  words <- str_extract_all(x, "\\b\\w+\\b")[[1]]
  
  for (w in words) {
    if (!is.na(w) && nchar(w) >= 6 && nchar(w) <= 9) {
      dist <- adist(tolower(w), "research")[1, 1]
      if (!is.na(dist) && dist > 0 && dist <= 2) {
        repl <- if (str_detect(w, "^[A-Z]")) "Research" else "research"
        x <- str_replace(x, fixed(w), repl)
      }
    }
  }
  x
}


df_responses_raw <- read.csv("data/local.drtp_contribs_survey_respondents.csv")


df_responses <- df_responses_raw |> 
  #convert to dates
  mutate(
    start_date = as.Date(start_date),
    end_date = as.Date(end_date),
  ) |> 
  # Coalesces job_title
  mutate(
    job_title = map_chr(job_title, fix_research_typo),
    job_title = str_remove(job_title, "\\(RSE\\)"),
    job_title = str_trim(job_title),
    job_title = str_replace(job_title, "RSE", "Research Software Engineer"),
    job_title = case_when(
      # str_detect(str_trim(job_title), "^RSE$") ~ "Research Software Engineer",
      str_detect(tolower(str_trim(job_title)), "^research software engineer$") ~ "Research Software Engineer",
      # str_detect(job_title, "Senior RSE") ~ "Senior Research Software Engineer",
      # str_detect(job_title, "Principal RSE") ~ "Principal Research Software Engineer",
      str_detect(job_title, "associate professor") ~ "Asociate Professor",
      str_detect(job_title, "Research Data$") ~ "Research Data Steward",
      .default = job_title
    ),
    job_title = as.factor(job_title),
    job_title = fct_infreq(job_title)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    job_category = case_when(
      str_detect(job_title, "Research Software Engineer") ~ "RSE",
      str_detect(job_title, "Data Steward") ~ "Data Steward",
      str_detect(job_title, "Community") ~ "Community Manager",
      str_detect(job_title, "Professor") ~ "Academic",
      .default = "Other"
    ),
    job_category = fct_infreq(as.factor(job_category))
  ) |> 
  # Reorder factors
  mutate(
    years_drtp = fct_relevel(
      as.factor(years_drtp), 
      "Never",
      "less than a year",
      "1-5 years",
      "5-9 years"
    )
  ) |> 
  # Filtering answers that are basically empty
  filter(progress > 50) |> 
  filter(if_any(10:-1, complete.cases))

df_responses_tmp <- df_responses |> 
  select(response_id, job_title, pedagogy_training)

df_trainings <- read.csv("data/local.drtp_contribs_survey_trainings.csv") |> 
  rename(
    training_audience = training_audience__selected_choice
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    training_direct_framework_mapping_raw = training_direct_framework_mapping,
    training_direct_framework_mapping = training_direct_framework_mapping |> 
    # Information and data technologies
    str_replace_all(fixed("Data Science: Application of analytical, statistical or machine learning techniques to extract insight and value from complex or large datasets (big data)"), "Data Science") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Data Management: Understanding and implementation of practices for data management, quality, accessibility, stewardship and compliance across data lifecycle"), "Data Management") |> 
    # Software engineering and development 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Web & mobile development: Design and development of responsive, secure, and user-centric applications across web and mobile platforms"), "Web & mobile development") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Software engineering methodologies & tools: Application of structured approaches, theory and supporting tools to plan, develop, test, and maintain high-quality software systems efficiently"), "Software engineering methodologies & tools") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Software/computer science concepts & theory: Foundational knowledge of computational principles and algorithms that inform software design, development and performance"), "Software/computer science concepts & theory") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("User Interface/User Experience (UI/UX) design: Creating intuitive, inclusive, and engaging digital experiences through thoughtful design and user-centered practices"), "User Interface/User Experience (UI/UX) design") |> 
    # ICT Infrastructure
    str_replace_all(fixed("HPC infrastructure: Knowledge of high-performance computing systems and practices that support intensive computational research and large-scale simulations"), "HPC infrastructure") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Web infrastructure: Design, deployment, and maintenance of the technologies that support robust, scalable, and secure online platforms and services"), "Web infrastructure") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Cloud infrastructure: Expertise in leveraging cloud platforms to enable flexible, scalable, and cost-effective computing, storage, and data services"), "Cloud infrastructure") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("General systems infrastructure: Broad understanding of digital infrastructure - including hardware, networks, and system integration that supports everyday operations and research"), "General systems infrastructure") |> 
    # Professional skills
    str_replace_all(fixed("Personal skills: Self-management capabilities such as initiative, adaptability, resilience, time management, and a commitment to continuous learning."), "Personal skills") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Interprersonal skills: Ability to build rapport, demonstrate empathy, navigate social dynamics, and communicate effectively in diverse professional settings"), "Interpersonal skills") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Teamwork and collaboration: Working constructively and inclusively with others to achieve shared goals, contribute to group problem-solving, and foster a positive team culture"), "Teamwork and collaboration") |> 
    # Leadership & management
    str_replace_all(fixed("People & team management: Guiding and supporting individuals and teams to achieve their potential, with attention to wellbeing, performance, and professional growth"), "People & team management") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Leadership: Setting direction, inspiring others, and making strategic decisions that align people and projects with broader institutional or organisational goals"), "Leadership") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Project management: Planning, coordinating, and delivering projects effectively within defined scope, time, and resource constraints, while managing risk and quality"), "Project management") |> 
    # Domain expertise & Research
    str_replace_all(fixed("Domain knowledge: Deep understanding of the concepts, challenges, and methodologies specific to a particular scientific field"), "Domain knowledge") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Research skills: Conducting rigorous inquiry, including problem formulation, experimental design, critical analysis, and dissemination of findings"), "Research skills") |> 
    # Communication
    str_replace_all(fixed("Verbal & written communication: Articulating complex ideas clearly and effectively through a range of formats and for varied audiences"), "Verbal & written communication") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Community & outreach: Engaging with wider communities through knowledge sharing, collaboration, and public engagement to increase the visibility and impact of work"), "Community & outreach") |> 
    str_replace_all(fixed("Training: Designing and delivering effective learning experiences that build skills, transfer knowledge, and support capacity and capability development across audiences"), "Training")
  )
```

# Survey (I)

About professionals involved in teaching

## Professional categories distributions

What are the DRTPs professions involved in teaching?

```{r}
df_responses |> 
  count(job_category, job_title, name = "count") |> 
  mutate(percentage = scales::percent(count / sum(count), accuracy = 0.1)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(area = count, fill = job_category, label = paste0(job_title,"\n (", percentage, ")" ), subgroup = job_category )) +
  geom_treemap(layout = "squarified", colour = "white") +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border(colour = "white", size = 2) +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_text(place = "centre", grow = TRUE,
                             alpha = 0.25, colour = "white",
                             fontface = "italic") +
  geom_treemap_text(place = "centre",size = 12) +
  labs(title = "Responses by job titles and categories") +
  guides(fill = "none")
```

## Pedagogical backgrounds {.smaller}

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| layout: [[60], [40]]
df_responses |>
  filter(!is.na(pedagogy_training)) |> 
  mutate(pedagogy_training = pedagogy_training |>
           str_replace_all(fixed("Yes, I have received significant training on teaching or pedagogy (e.g. Degree, PGCert, etc.)"), "Significant pedagogy training") |>
           str_replace_all(fixed("Yes, I have received some training on teaching or pedagogy (e.g. dedicated course)"), "Some pedagogy training") |>
           str_replace_all(fixed("Yes, I have received training on how to teach technical skills (e.g. carpentries)"), "Technical teaching training") |>
           str_replace_all(fixed("No, I have not received any training on teaching or pedagogy"), "No training for trainers")
  ) |> 
  separate_longer_delim(pedagogy_training, delim = ",") |> 
  mutate(pedagogy_training = fct_infreq(as.factor(pedagogy_training))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(pedagogy_training), fill = job_category)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Training for trainers received",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  )


df_responses |> 
  filter(!is.na(degree_max)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = degree_max)) + 
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum degree earned",
    y = NULL
  )
```

- dRTPs have received extensive HE training

- dRTPs are largely trained to be technical trainers (carpentries), but

  - Significant amount of them have not received any training in pedagogy or training Digital Research Competencies
  - Only a fraction have significant training on pedagogy (pgCERT, FHEA).

- **dRTPs are experts in their domains and Digital Research Competencies, but not necessarily on teaching/pedagogy**

## Stances in relation to tech and pedagogy

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
df_responses |> 
  select(starts_with("statements_")) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything()) |> 
  filter(!is.na(value)) |> 
  count(name, value) |> 
  mutate(
    value = fct_relevel(
      as.factor(value), 
      "Strongly agree",
      "Somewhat agree",
      "Neither agree nor disagree",
      "Somewhat disagree"
    ),
    value_num = as.numeric(value),
    name = str_remove(name, "statements_"),
    name = str_replace_all(name, "_", " "),
    name = fct_reorder(name, value_num * n, .fun = sum)
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = n)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = NULL
  )
```

## How's being taught?

Maybe because of lack of pedagogical training... (consider creating a narrative in the slides)

```{r}
df_trainings |> 
  mutate(
    training_type = str_remove(training_type, "\\(e\\.g.*?\\)"),
    # training_type = str_replace_all(training_type, "\\(e\\.g.", "\n\\(e\\.g.")
  ) |> 
  separate_longer_delim(training_type, delim = ",") |> 
  mutate(training_type = fct_infreq(as.factor(training_type))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(training_type), fill = training_delivery)) +

    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  )
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
- Part of a degree curricula (either UG or PG), separating between core or optional modules.

- Formal (e.g. compulsory training for a job such as accessing HPC services).

- Informal: any course or workshop not fiting in any previous category.
:::

```{r}
  mutate(training_type = fct_infreq(as.factor(training_type))) |> 
  mutate(
    training_role = str_remove_all(training_role, "\\(i\\.e.*?\\)")
  ) |> 
  separate_longer_delim(training_role, delim = ",") |> 
  mutate(training_role = fct_rev(fct_infreq(training_role))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = training_role, fill = job_category)) +
  geom_bar() + 
  facet_wrap(~training_type) +
  labs(
    title = "Role played in trainings (by training type)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  )

```

- dRTPs lead on informal training
- dRTPs are less involved in degree's curricula, and when they are, they tend to have a supporting role

```{r}
df_trainings |> 
  select(starts_with("training_tasks__")) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything()) |> 
  mutate(
    name = str_remove(name, "training_tasks__"),
    name = str_replace_all(name, "_", " "),
    name = fct_reorder(as.factor(name), value)
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(y = name, x = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "darkgrey") +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Time spent per task",
    y = NULL,
    x = "%"
  )

```
